title: Camping Quest Unearths 390-Million-Year-Old Cosmic Scar in Quebec
summary: An amateur astronomer seeking a camping spot in Quebec accidentally discovered a previously unknown, 390-million-year-old impact crater. Scientists later confirmed the 25-kilometer-wide structure's cosmic origin with shatter cones, providing a rare glimpse into Earth's ancient history.
content:
It began with a search for a tranquil camping spot in Quebec. What amateur astronomer Robert Saint-Louis stumbled upon instead was a geological marvel: a 25-kilometer-wide, 390-million-year-old impact crater, previously unknown to science. This isn't just a pretty circle on a map; it's a profound window into Earth's tumultuous past, unearthed by pure serendipity.

Saint-Louis's keen eye, while sifting through satellite imagery for recreational purposes, spotted an unusual circular formation. His curiosity piqued, he shared his findings, leading a team of professional scientists to investigate. Their ground expedition yielded definitive proof: shatter cones. These distinct geological formations are only created under the extreme pressures of a meteorite impact, unequivocally confirming the structure’s cosmic origin. The discovery of these cones cemented the circular feature as a colossal impact scar, blasted into our planet roughly 390 million years ago.

At 25 kilometers in diameter, this ancient behemoth, now dubbed the "Saint-Louis Impact Crater," is a significant addition to Earth's known impact record. Craters of this age and size are incredibly rare due to millennia of erosion, tectonic plate movements, and sediment deposition, which often erase such ancient scars. Its remarkable preservation offers invaluable data for geologists studying Earth's early history and the frequency of extraterrestrial bombardments during the Devonian period. Moreover, it underscores the profound contributions that citizen scientists continue to make in fields traditionally dominated by academic institutions.

From a simple desire for a weekend escape to unearthing a piece of planetary history, Robert Saint-Louis’s accidental discovery is a powerful reminder that our world, even in its most mapped corners, still holds breathtaking secrets. It’s a testament to the fact that sometimes, the greatest scientific revelations begin with a mere glance at a satellite map and an insatiable curiosity.
keyTakeaways: An amateur astronomer discovered a 390-million-year-old, 25-kilometer-wide impact crater in Quebec while searching satellite maps for camping spots.
Scientists confirmed the crater's cosmic origin by finding shatter cones, geological formations unique to high-pressure impacts.
The discovery offers rare insights into Earth's ancient history and the frequency of extraterrestrial bombardments during the Devonian period, highlighting the value of citizen science.

title: From Rockets to Retail: Jupiter Exchange Blasts Off with Tokenized SpaceX, HYPE, ZEC Perps on Solana
summary: Solana's leading DEX aggregator, Jupiter Exchange, has significantly expanded its perpetual futures offerings to include tokenized SpaceX shares, Hyperliquid's HYPE, and Zcash. This move, powered by a new orderbook engine, democratizes access to unique assets and marks a bold new frontier for decentralized finance on Solana.
content:
The decentralized finance (DeFi) landscape on Solana just got a significant jolt, blurring the lines between traditional and crypto markets in an unprecedented way. Jupiter Exchange, the network’s premier decentralized exchange aggregator, has dramatically expanded its perpetual futures lineup.

This isn't just another crypto token launch; it's a leap into uncharted territory, now offering perps for tokenized shares of Elon Musk’s private space exploration giant, SpaceX (SPCX), alongside Hyperliquid’s native HYPE token, and the privacy-focused Zcash (ZEC). This audacious move means users can now gain exposure to the volatile, high-stakes world of space innovation, even if indirectly, through a tokenized derivative on the Solana blockchain.

The inclusion of SPCX is particularly noteworthy, as direct investment in SpaceX is typically a domain reserved for accredited investors. Alongside this, HYPE, a token associated with a rapidly growing perpetual exchange, adds a layer of inter-DeFi connectivity, while Zcash provides a well-established crypto asset to the mix. These additions aren’t merely about increasing trading volume; they represent a concerted effort to broaden the appeal and utility of Solana’s burgeoning DeFi ecosystem, potentially reshaping crypto trading dynamics.

Powering this ambitious expansion is a brand-new orderbook engine, a critical upgrade designed to handle the increased complexity and liquidity demands of these diverse markets. This robust technical backbone ensures efficient price discovery and a resilient trading infrastructure, a necessity as Jupiter continues to push the boundaries of what’s tradable on a decentralized exchange. By bringing such varied and previously inaccessible assets into the perpetual futures fold, Jupiter Exchange isn't just innovating; it's democratizing financial instruments and setting a new precedent for the future of decentralized trading on Solana's high-speed, low-cost network.
keyTakeaways: Jupiter Exchange expanded its perpetual futures markets on Solana to include tokenized SpaceX shares (SPCX), Hyperliquid's HYPE token, and Zcash (ZEC).
The expansion aims to democratize access to unique assets, particularly private company shares like SpaceX, previously inaccessible to most retail investors.
A new, robust orderbook engine underpins these diverse perpetual markets, enhancing Solana's DeFi trading infrastructure and efficiency.

title: Science Museum Blasts Off with Pokémon Space Trail, Teaming Up with ESA for Out-of-This-World Fun
summary: The Science Museum in London is launching an immersive Pokémon Space Trail next month, celebrating the franchise's anniversaries with an educational twist. This unique collaboration with the European Space Agency promises exclusive merchandise and an interactive journey for fans of all ages.
content:
London's fervent Pokémon fanbase is about to receive another stellar treat, building on a year already rich with celebratory events. As the iconic franchise marks its 30th anniversary and the groundbreaking mobile game Pokémon GO hits its tenth year, the festivities are culminating in an unexpected and thrilling collaboration: a Pokémon Space Trail at the prestigious Science Museum.

This isn't just another themed exhibition. Partnering with the European Space Agency (ESA), the Science Museum is set to launch an immersive experience that marries the whimsical world of Pokémon with the awe-inspiring realities of space exploration. Visitors will embark on an interactive journey, discovering fascinating facts about our solar system, distant galaxies, and the vital work of astronauts, all while encountering their favorite pocket monsters in an entirely new context.

The trail, designed to be both educational and entertaining, promises to challenge participants with 'missions' akin to those faced by real space explorers. From learning about celestial bodies to understanding the challenges of living in zero gravity, the experience aims to ignite curiosity in science and technology for all ages. And, as expected with any major Pokémon event, a dedicated pop-up shop will offer an array of exclusive, limited-edition merchandise, perfect for collectors eager to commemorate this unique cosmic adventure.

This unprecedented fusion of pop culture and scientific discovery underscores a growing trend in engaging new generations with STEM subjects. By leveraging the immense appeal of Pokémon, the Science Museum and ESA are crafting an accessible entry point into complex topics, proving that learning about the universe can be as captivating as catching a rare shiny. Mark your calendars for next month; this might just be the most exciting mission of the year.
keyTakeaways: The Science Museum in London is hosting a new 'Pokémon Space Trail' starting next month.
The immersive experience is a unique collaboration with the European Space Agency (ESA), blending pop culture with space education.
The event celebrates Pokémon's 30th birthday and Pokémon GO's 10th anniversary, featuring exclusive merchandise and interactive learning.
